sources.title: Coningham, Manuel, Davis and Gunawardhana, Archaeology and Cosmopolitanism in Early Historic and Medieval Sri Lanka (2017)
sources.note: Open UCL Press book, chapter 1, printed pages 19 to 43. Downloaded and read locally: pages 26 to 27 for excavation and trade; page 32 for monastic politics. Entire book treated as one source budget. The disputed earliest pottery inscriptions are not used to claim an invention of writing.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Sacred City of Anuradhapura
sources.note: Institutional listing read through indexed original. Buddhist sacred history is identified as tradition. The map interval is local imported metadata, not UNESCO chronology. The city continued beyond 800.

sources.title: ICOMOS, Sacred City of Anuradhapura evaluation (1982)
sources.note: Both PDF pages read. Page 2 supports monumental patronage and stupa architecture. Do not adopt its dated rhetoric about ethnic purity, its simplistic abandonment narrative, or the English 993 B.C. typographical error.

sources.title: Coningham, Davis, Gunawardhana and Manuel, From village to state, and back again (online 2026)
sources.note: Full scholarly article obtained as publicly served HTML and read locally; local village.pdf has an HTML body despite the filename. Rice-processing section, Figures 1 to 3 and Table 1 establish nambiliya in Early Historic and later assemblages. No later percentage is attributed to the pre-800 period. Conclusion distinguishes de-urbanization from disappearance and recognizes other island polities. DOI 10.1080/00438243.2026.2664414.

sources.title: Abeywardana, Bebermeier and Schütt, Ancient Water Management and Governance in the Dry Zone of Sri Lanka (2018)
sources.note: Full open PDF downloaded from publisher and read. Sections 3.1 to 3.3 and Tables 2 to 4 distinguish tanks, water shares, ownership and early occupations. Later ninth-century and subsequent rules are not projected into the map period.

sources.title: Siddham IN03200, Timbirivava rock inscription of Anulabi; edition and translation by Senarath Paranavitana
sources.note: Direct public HTML, embedded TEI and translation tab saved and read. Epigraphia Zeylanica 4, pages 223 to 228, no. 28. First line has Mitayaha jita Anuḷabi; translation identifies Anulabi as daughter of Mitaya. Gift is income from a share of a family tank. Third-century date follows Paranavitana identifying Mekavana Aba as Gothabhaya; Bell had proposed a different royal identification. Transliteration is reproduced, not an invented Brahmi rendering. All tabs count as one source.

sources.title: Siddham IN03225, Timbirivava Rock Inscription 3
sources.note: Direct public HTML and translation downloaded and read. Undated inscription assigned to fifth or sixth century by script and language; elder brother pays 100 kahavanas to free Aba. This findspot south of Maradanmaduva differs from Anulabi inscription at Veheragala.

sources.title: Faxian, A Record of Buddhistic Kingdoms, chapters 38 to 40; James Legge translation (1886)
sources.note: Primary travel narrative read in full relevant chapters through web extraction. Chapter 38: white-silk fan, preaching halls, tooth festival; chapter 40: two-year stay and acquired texts. Observer reports are attributed to him, not treated as a statistical survey of island life. Entire book is one source budget.

sources.title: W. I. Siriweera, Sanitation and Health Care in Ancient Sri Lanka (2003/2004)
sources.note: University of Peradeniya repository PDF downloaded and read. Printed pages 1 to 4 discuss social bias of remains and Abhayagiri sanitation; page 7 maternity homes attributed to Upatissa I; page 8 medical plants under Aggabodhi VII. Study spans through the thirteenth century. Toilet passage explicitly says its structures are not securely dated before 800 in this study. Later Mihintale hospital plan is not claimed as evidence within this map interval.

sources.title: Central Cultural Fund, Sigiriya Rock Fortress
sources.note: Institutional site read through indexed original; direct web fetch fails. Kashyapa reign 477 to 495, Moggallana, return to monastery; paintings and differing interpretations. The page geology and claims of a world-first landscape garden are not used.

sources.title: Central Province Tourism Department, Sigiriya Gardens
sources.note: Official department page directly read. Water gardens, underground conduits, circular limestone fountain plates, relation to lake and moats. Present operation during rains is a conservation-site observation, not evidence of unchanged operation at every intervening date.

sources.title: Gill Juleff, An ancient wind-powered iron smelting technology in Sri Lanka, Nature 379 (1996)
sources.note: Author abstract directly read: western hill/ridge margins, monsoon winds, replica trials, high-carbon steel, first-millennium industry. Full subscription article not accessed.

sources.title: Brett Leslie Freese, Wind-Powered Furnaces, Archaeology 49.5 (1996)
sources.note: Archaeological Institute of America report directly read; reports excavation director Gill Juleff and field trials, with seventh-century earliest use and eleventh-century continuation. Used for dating alongside Juleff original research abstract; speculative Damascus-sword connection omitted.

batchIdentityNotes.finding: Exact missing indexed Historical Basemaps record, imported -500 to 800 with circa true. Fourteen decoded snapshots have effectively the same island outline, bounds 79.674 to 81.867 east and 5.932 to 9.686 north. This is a coarse island-wide label, not evidence for a single state, uniform ethnicity or invariant royal control. No aliases assigned. Later sinhalese-kingdoms (800 to 900), sinhalese-kingdom (1279 to 1492), sinhalese-kingdoms-1492 and Ceylon/Sri Lanka records remain distinct. Earlier archaeology and later sanitation are explicitly contextualized. See identities.json.
